guide.title: How to pair a tablet at a pizzeria
guide.lead: Once per tablet, about a minute. You need a tablet with internet and this workspace — on a computer or a phone.

step1.title: Issue a code
step1.text: In Stations, open the station where the tablet will stand and press “Pair a tablet”. Four digits appear.
step1.drawerText: Press “Pair a tablet” above — four digits appear.

step2.title: Open the address on the tablet
step2.text: Type this address in the tablet's browser. It helps to add it to the tablet's home screen.

step3.title: Type the code
step3.text: The tablet shows a four-digit field: type the code the cabinet showed in step 1 and press “Pair”. The code is valid for {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} and works once.

step4.title: Done
step4.text: The tablet opens the station checklist right away and keeps opening it on its own — after a restart and without a new code. The paired tablet appears on the station card.

trouble.title: If it did not work
trouble.expired: The tablet says “This code does not work” — the code expired or was already used. Issue a new one: the old one simply stops working.
trouble.tooOften: “Too many attempts” — wait, the tablet tells you how many minutes.
trouble.unpaired: “This tablet is not paired” — it was unpaired here or its station was deleted. Issue a new code and type it.
trouble.nothing: The tablet is paired but says “Nothing to fill in right now” — the station has no checklist, or it is not its time yet.
trouble.move: To move a tablet to another station, issue a code for the new station and type it on the same tablet: the old pairing is removed on its own.

checklists.why: A checklist is what a team member checks at a station during a shift.
checklists.what: This is where checklists are created and edited: items, the shift window, blocks from the library. The kitchen sees only the published version, so a draft is safe to edit.
checklists.next: Once published, the checklist opens from its station's QR sticker, and what gets filled in shows up in Statistics.

stations.why: A station is the place in the kitchen where a checklist is filled in: by phone from the sticker, or from a paired tablet.
stations.what: Here you can see what covers each station. A station with no checklist is marked — its sticker opens onto nothing. Tick stations in the column to roll out a copy of a template to them or to print their stickers in one go.
stations.next: Open a station to find its checklist, its sticker and tablet pairing.

templates.why: A template is how we see the ideal shift. It prescribes nothing.
templates.what: Take a template and adapt it: your copy lives its own life. When the template is updated, your copy shows what changed, and you take what fits.
templates.next: A template you have taken is rolled out to stations in Stations.

library.why: A block is a set of items that repeats across checklists.
library.what: A block's items are edited here, in one place, and the change appears in every draft the block is inserted into. Published versions do not change.
library.next: Insert the block into a checklist in the editor and publish a version — that is when the change reaches the kitchen.

feed.why: This is where you see how checklists go in the pizzerias: what is filled today, what was missed and where critical items fail.
feed.what: Countries on the left, tiles of their pizzerias on the right with today’s status and figures for 7 or 30 days. A tile opens the pizzeria: all its checklists with statistics, alarms and the submission feed.
feed.next: Found a weak spot? Open the submission card, fix the checklist in Checklists or look into the station in Stations.

catalog.why: Countries, pizzerias and their stations — the base of the network: everything else relies on them.
catalog.what: Add a pizzeria and its stations. Head office edits the whole network; a partner edits the pizzerias and stations of their own countries.
catalog.next: A new station appears in Stations: put a checklist on it and print its sticker.

partners.why: A partner is a pizzeria network that works in the cabinet with its own countries.
partners.what: Create a partner account here and give it countries: signed in with its own login, the partner sees only those. Passwords are changed and reset and accounts removed here too.
partners.next: Hand the login and password to the partner yourself — the product does not send them.
